title: Stock Market Today Live: Stock to buy today: Markets likely to open flat to positive despite FPI selling, global headwinds - The HinduBusinessLine
text:

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates: Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 13th October 2026.

The rise has taken the share price well above a key resistance level of ₹4,880. The region between ₹4,900 and ₹4,800 is a good support zone for the stock now. Moving Average indicators are also giving good bullish signal.

Netweb Technologies India share price can rise to ₹5,450-₹5,500 in the coming weeks. Traders can buy Netweb Technologies India shares now at ₹5,001. Accumulate on dips at ₹4,940. Keep the stop-loss at ₹4,740 initially. Trail the stop-loss up to ₹5,080 as soon as the stock goes up to ₹5,160. Revise the stop-loss higher to ₹5,230 and ₹5,320 when the share price touches ₹5,280 and ₹5,390 respectively. Exit the long positions at ₹5,440.

Indian stocks open flat amid volatility and selling pressure, with inflation, crude costs, and geopolitics weighing on gains.

* Spot gold was down 0.2% at $4,161.81 per ounce ⁠by 0015 GMT after hitting a one-week peak in the previous session.

* US gold futures for ‌December delivery fell 0.1% at $4,186.60.

* The US dollar lingered near an ‌18-month high, making dollar-denominated metals more expensive ‌for ⁠holders of other currencies.

Gold prices were subdued on Tuesday, with market focus on upcoming US inflation prints for fresh signals on the Federal ‌Reserve’s interest-rate trajectory.

Company announces buyback of 1,562,500 equity shares at ₹960 each; buyback to open on October 15, 2026 and close on October 22, 2026; total buyback amount not exceeding ₹150 crore

- Investment amount of INR 1.62 Cr completed on 12th October, 2026

- Investment made via subscription to equity shares of the SPV

- Investment follows the Share Subscription and Shareholders Agreement (SSSHA) executed with Hero Rooftop Energy Private Limited

- Investment intended to enable solar power usage and reduce energy costs

- Aimed at supporting environmental sustainability and carbon neutrality initiatives

Buzzing Tuesday stock movers: AI partnerships, fraud flags, leadership shifts, big project wins, and renewable/defence bets across multiple listed firms.

* Bajaj Healthcare (BAJAJHEA): Sells Dahej unit for ~INR146.7m to SPA Vet, Indosol

* Bank of India (BOI): Future Enterprise’s INR5.75b NPA declared as fraud

* Fortis Healthcare (FORH): To invest in captive solar SPV in Haryana

* HCL Technologies (HCLT): 2Q Net Income +21% Y/y to INR51.3b, Beats Estimates

* ICICI Prudential AMC (ICICIAMC): 2Q Net Income +6.1% Y/y to INR8.89b, Meets Estimates

* Indian Hotels (IH): Signs 47 hotels and 20 hotel openings in first half of FY27

* Indian Oil Corp. (IOCL): Seeks Spot Cargo for Late-Oct. Delivery: LNG TENDER

* L&T Technology (LTTS): Launches EI Lab for manufacturing & operations

* Nazara Technologies (NAZARA): To invest up to $77m in UK unit; Arun Agrawal named new CFO succeeding Rakesh Shah

* RBL Bank (RBK): 2Q Net Income INR4.82b, Beats Estimates

* REC Ltd. (RECL): To sell 2 Power Transmission SPVs; Sells Lakadia II to Power Grid (PWGR) and Jam Khambhaliya Jamnagar unit to Ceigall India

* Reliance Industries (RELIANCE): India Top Court Asks Mumbai Agency to Refund $68M to Reliance

* Sun Pharma (SUNP): Approves Raising Up to $1 Billion Selling Bonds

* TD Power Systems (TDPS): Closes QIP at issue price of INR775/share

* Vikran Engineering (VIKRAN): Says unit NOPL Solar gets up to INR29.4b financing from IREDA

Asian stocks declined as the artificial intelligence trade, one of the hottest corners of the market this year, came under renewed pressure ahead of a key earnings season.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index lost 0.9%, set for its weakest close since mid-August, as shares retreated in South Korea and Japan.

13 Stocks Closed at Fresh Lifetime Highs Today

* RBL Bank reported 2QFY27 PAT of INR4.8b (7% miss, up 90% QoQ/170% YoY) amid higher than expected provisioning.

* NII grew 37% YoY/29% QoQ to INR21.3b (in-line). NIMs improved by 48bp QoQ to 4.61% in 2QFY27 (our est of 4.31%) led by full impact of capital infusion from Emirates NBD.

* Other income rose 12% QoQ and 16% YoY to INR10.8b (4% miss).

* Total revenues thus were up 23% QoQ/29% YoY to INR32.1b (in-line).

* Opex was up 3% YoY/ 7% QoQ to INR18.1b (6% lower than MOLSe).

* PPoP thus grew by 51% QoQ (up 92% YoY) to INR14b (8% beat).

* Provisions came in higher at INR7.7b (up 28% QoQ/ 53% YoY, 25% above our MOSLe) as the management created additional std. provision of 11bps.

* Advances grew 42% YoY/22% QoQ while deposits grew 34% YoY/down 25% QoQ, led by surplus FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation of USD 3.4b.

* Gross NPA ratio declined by 28bp QoQ to 1.02%, while NNPA ratio declined by 8bp QoQ to 0.29%. PCR stood at 71.5%.

* RoA (annualised) stood at 0.92% in 2QFY27.
